content.text: The reactivity series is an evidence ladder: metals ranked by how they behave with water, with dilute hydrochloric or sulfuric acid, and in displacement reactions. Potassium and sodium float and fizz at the top; copper, silver and gold sit quietly at the bottom. Carbon and hydrogen are not metals but ride the ladder as reference points - carbon because it pulls oxygen off oxides, hydrogen because metals above it pop into acids.
